shared_context.patient: A 1-year-old girl is brought to a neurologist due to increasing seizure frequency over the past 2 months. She recently underwent a neurology evaluation which revealed hypsarrhythmia on electroencephalography (EEG) with a mix of slow waves, multifocal spikes, and asynchrony. Her parents have noticed the patient occasionally stiffens and spreads her arms at home. She was born at 38-weeks gestational age without complications. She has no other medical problems. Her medications consist of lamotrigine and valproic acid. Her temperature is 98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 90/75 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respirations are 22/min. Physical exam reveals innumerable hypopigmented macules on the skin and an irregularly shaped, thickened, and elevated plaque on the lower back.

atoms.1: This presentation is characteristic of infantile spasms.
atoms.2: Infantile spasms are also known as West syndrome.
atoms.3: Infantile spasms are often associated with a poor developmental prognosis.
atoms.4: Hypsarrhythmia on EEG is a hallmark of infantile spasms.
atoms.5: This physical behavior is indicative of infantile spasms.
atoms.6: Infantile spasms manifest as brief, involuntary muscle contractions, often involving the arms.
atoms.7: Valproic acid is an antiepileptic drug.
atoms.8: There is no indication that lamotrigine and valproic acid are contributing to her current condition.
atoms.9: The skin findings are suggestive of tuberous sclerosis complex.
atoms.10: Tuberous sclerosis complex is a genetic disorder.
atoms.11: Tuberous sclerosis complex is characterized by the growth of non-cancerous tumors in various organs.
atoms.12: Tuberous sclerosis complex includes the growth of non-cancerous tumors in the skin, brain, and other areas.
atoms.13: Tuberous sclerosis complex is associated with a range of neurological manifestations.
atoms.14: Neurological manifestations of tuberous sclerosis complex include seizures.
atoms.15: Neurological manifestations of tuberous sclerosis complex include intellectual disability.
atoms.16: Neurological manifestations of tuberous sclerosis complex include autism spectrum disorders.
atoms.17: Tuberous sclerosis complex has been associated with cardiac rhabdomyoma.
atoms.18: Cardiac rhabdomyoma is a type of benign heart tumor.
atoms.19: The correct answer is: A) Cardiac rhabdomyoma.
